title: Third-party scorer kwargs: destination keys are rejected at any nesting depth, including [key, value] pair lists and ensemble/MemAlign sub-scorers; non-object kwargs are rejected
answers: Why is my TruLens Coherence or RAGAS judge rejected when I pass api_base or base_url in kwargs?
Can a client choose a custom judge endpoint through a scorer's kwargs, and if not, how is it configured?
Where is the check for destination keys nested in completion_kwargs or model_kwargs?
An ensemble containing a third-party judge returns 400 even though the top-level scorer looks clean. Why?
body:
Path: mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data handles the third_party_scorer_data payloads for TruLens, RAGAS, DeepEval and Phoenix scorers (their kwargs, completion_kwargs, model_kwargs) on the register, invoke and evaluate paths. It walks the whole payload through mlflow/utils/validation.py:_iter_third_party_scorer_data, so sub-scorers inside ensemble_scorer_data.scorers and memory_augmented_judge_data.base_judge are checked too.
Rule: The rejected keys are the GATEWAY_DESTINATION_KEYS constant (api_base, base_url, model_list, fallbacks, custom_llm_provider), found recursively by mlflow/utils/validation.py:_find_destination_keys. That helper also treats a two-item [key, value] list as a key, because dict() accepts such lists. kwargs must be a JSON object or null, since deserialization runs dict(kwargs or {}). Reuse the same constant and the same walk when a new third-party scorer or wrapper type is added; do not check only top-level kwargs.
Symptom: A judge with kwargs written as [["api_base", url]], or with api_base nested under completion_kwargs, or wrapped in an ensemble, passed a top-level-only check, and the LLM client then connected to the caller-chosen host.
Constraints: Only these five destination keys are blocked; other options such as threshold or temperature still pass. To point a judge at a custom endpoint, configure it on the server through a gateway:/<name> endpoint or the provider's environment variables.
applies: Validation of third_party_scorer_data for TruLens, RAGAS, DeepEval and Phoenix scorers, including ensembles and MemAlign judges, on any server path that accepts serialized scorers.
says: Registering an evaluation judge with a custom endpoint URL is rejected with an error
Ensemble scorer fails validation when a nested sub-judge specifies a custom endpoint
Model evaluation rejects custom parameters that specify an external model provider host
Why does configuring a custom destination address for evaluation scorers return an error
Evaluation requests fail because the judge contains blocked destination network settings
search: Validation of third_party_scorer_data in mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data recursively rejects GATEWAY_DESTINATION_KEYS (api_base, base_url, model_list, fallbacks, custom_llm_provider) at any nesting depth, including two-item [key, value] lists, completion_kwargs, model_kwargs, and sub-scorers walked via _iter_third_party_scorer_data. Scorer kwargs must be a JSON object or null, while non-destination options like threshold and temperature remain allowed. This applies on register, invoke, and evaluate paths for TruLens, RAGAS, DeepEval, Phoenix, ensemble, and MemAlign judges; custom endpoints must be configured on the server via gateway:/<name> or provider environment variables.
